conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I’m Dr. Lee. I’ve been reviewing why you came in tonight. You’re here for nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain again—similar to past visits. How are you feeling right now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m in a lot of pain. It’s my pancreas—it’s always the same. I need something for pain and something to help me sleep.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. We’ve given you some hydromorphone for pain and a little diazepam to help you relax. But your blood sugar was high—395—so we started an insulin drip to bring it down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I didn’t want insulin at first. I can manage it myself. I know my body.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You did refuse it initially, but then agreed. We also gave fluids and anti-nausea meds—30 mg of Compazine total. Your labs showed an elevated anion gap—23—which suggests mild ketoacidosis. That’s why the insulin is important.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I’m in DKA again? But I feel okay now. Can’t I just go home and handle it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your anion gap has started to close, which means the acidosis is improving. But we’d like to keep you a bit longer to make sure your sugar stabilizes and you’re safe to leave.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I really want to leave. I promise I’ll check my sugars and take my insulin. I’ve been doing this for years.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I know you’re capable. You showed us you can draw up insulin correctly. But we’re concerned because you’ve had multiple admissions for this. Are you getting support at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My guardian checks in, but I live alone. I just need my meds and some rest. The pain gets worse when I’m stressed here.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I hear that. We also saw your potassium was low—3.0—so we offered to replace it, but you declined. That can make you feel worse and affect your heart.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t want more IVs. I’ll eat something when I get home. I’m not staying if you’re going to push more treatments.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We respect your choice. Since your anion gap has normalized and you’re alert and able to manage your insulin, we’re comfortable letting you leave against medical advice.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’ll be careful. I know what happens if I don’t.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re giving you 15 units of long-acting insulin to take now, and you should continue your usual regimen—70 units at bedtime and lispro with meals.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’ll do that. And I’ll follow up with my doctor if things get bad.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Please do. And if the abdominal pain worsens or you can’t keep fluids down, come back right away. Your chronic pancreatitis and gastroparesis make this tricky.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know. But I’ll be okay. I just needed a little relief and to get out of here.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Alright. We’ll discharge you home now. Take care, and please reach out if you need help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just confirming—you’re leaving against medical advice, but you understand the risks of stopping treatment early, especially with DKA and chronic pain issues?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I understand. I’m responsible for my own care. I’ll monitor everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve documented that. Please sign here to confirm you’re leaving AMA.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Done. I appreciate your help, even if I’m leaving early.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take this information with you—your insulin doses, warning signs, and when to seek care. Stay safe.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’re here if you need us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll keep that in mind.
